name: Two For The Trails Grant
summary: Annual grants from a non-alcoholic brewer to nonprofits for shovel-ready outdoor projects such as habitat restoration, invasive species removal, waterway protection and trail work. Projects need land manager approval.
reporting: A brief mid-year report and a final report will be required from each grant recipient.

eligibility.rule: Be registered as a 501(c)3 if US-based
Have a project rooted in outdoor conservation or maintenance
Have a shovel-ready project approved by land managers
Have public access if the project is primarily on private land
Have no core purpose rooted in government, politics, or religion

documents: Completed W9, or W8 for non-US applicants
IRS tax exempt determination letter, or similar document for non-US applicants
Latest Form 990 filed with the IRS, or similar document for non-US applicants

applicant_types.quote: Must be a registered nonprofit organization.

geography.quote: Any international nonprofit may apply, although we give priority to projects in regions in which we operate (USA, Canada, United Kingdom, and EU).

amount.quote: The funds awarded range from $500 to $50,000, with an average of $5,000 to $10,000 per grant.

reporting.quote: A brief mid-year report and a final report will be required from each grant recipient.

eligibility.quote: Must be a registered nonprofit organization.
United States-based organizations must be registered 501(c)3
While your organization's core mission does not need to be rooted in outdoor conservation or maintenance, your project must be.
Fund shovel-ready projects or campaigns (not in planning stages) and must be approved by land managers
Fund a project on primarily private land unless it is given public access
Whose core purpose is rooted in government, politics, or religion

after_award.quote: A brief mid-year report and a final report will be required from each grant recipient.

documents.quote: Certificate of Insurance evidencing at least the following coverages:

Completed form W9 (or W8 for non-US applicants) • Copy of your IRS tax exempt determination letter (or similar document for non-US applicants) • Copy of your latest Form 990 filed with the IRS (or similar document for non-US applicants) • Timeline of the project
